name: Hohe Mut Bahn Obergurgl
kurzbeschreibung: The Hohe Mut Bahn in Obergurgl at 2,670 m: spectacular viewing platform with 360-degree views of 21 three-thousand-metre peaks and the Gurgler glacier expanse.
beschreibung:
Overview

The state-of-the-art Hohe Mut Bahn departs from the world-famous mountaineering and winter sports resort of Obergurgl in the rear Ötztal (Imst district) at an altitude of 1,930 metres. Across two sections, the comfortable 8-seater gondola lift ascends over 740 vertical metres, carrying guests up to the prominent mountain ridge of the Hohe Mut at an elevation of 2,670 metres above sea level. Regarded as one of the most spectacular viewpoint summits in the entire Eastern Alps, the ridge reveals a breathtaking 360-degree glacier panorama dominated by 21 ice-crowned peaks exceeding 3,000 metres and the mighty tongues of the Rotmoosferner and Gurgler Ferner glaciers.

Glacier Panorama, Biosphere Reserve & Alpine History

The Hohe Mut has exerted a magical fascination since the dawn of alpine tourism: from the expansive panoramic terrace of the stylish Hohe Mut Alm Restaurant at 2,670 metres, views stretch across the pristine high-alpine valleys of the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve Gurgler Kamm. Striking mountain summits such as the Hintere Schwärze (3,624 m), the Schalfkogel (3,537 m), and the Granatenkogel rise majestically into the sky. For nature lovers and science enthusiasts, the area is of profound importance: in summer, an instructive glacier educational trail explains alpine glaciology, permafrost soils, glacial retreat, and the adaptation strategies of alpine pioneer plants such as the glacier buttercup (Ranunculus glacialis). Obergurgl achieved historic worldwide fame in May 1931, when Swiss stratosphere pioneer Auguste Piccard made an emergency landing in his hot-air balloon directly on the Gurgler Ferner following his world altitude record – informational display boards at the mountain station commemorate this daring rescue. For hikers, the Hohe Mut serves as the starting point for rewarding high-alpine tours to the Zirbenwaldhütte, the Schönwieshütte, or through the Rotmoostal valley.

Visit & Getting There

The Hohe Mut Bahn operates during the summer season from mid-June to mid-September daily from 09:00 to 16:30 (in winter it provides access to demanding mogul slopes and deep-snow terrain). Fares for summer 2025/2026 (round-trip ascent and descent to the mountain station): adults approx. €32.00, children and youths (born 2010–2018) approx. €18.00, young children under 6 years ride free. Holders of the regional Ötztal Inside Summer Card use the cable car completely free of charge! Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Ötztal), continue along the Ötztalstraße B186 for approximately 50 km up the valley through Sölden directly to Obergurgl; parking is available in the parking garage at the village entrance or at the cable car stations. By public transport: ÖBB train to Ötztal railway station, from where VVT bus route 4194 runs every half hour directly to the Obergurgl Zentrum / Hotel Hochfirst stop (approx. a three-minute walk to the valley station).

Tips

The gondola lift and the Hohe Mut Alm Restaurant with its barrier-free viewing platform are fully accessible for wheelchairs and prams. At an altitude of 2,670 m, alpine weather can change rapidly even in midsummer; warm, windproof clothing and sturdy footwear are strictly essential. On your way back down, be sure to visit the protected, centuries-old Obergurgler Zirbenwald (natural stone pine monument) on the valley floor.
